thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert: multiple 5xx spikes observed from us-west edge pool (edgepool-7). Alert threshold crossed at ~1712345600. Auto-page sent to SRE and Eng-GW.

oncall-ben: I'm on it — looking at dashboards now. Can someone paste the top error logs?

sre_maria: grabbing logs, seeing lots of 503 and 504 with 'upstream queue full' and 'connection reset by peer'. snippet:```
[usw1-edge-7] 2024-04-05T12:34:10Z GET /v1/generate 503 "upstream_queue_overflow" src=10.2.7.44
[usw1-edge-7] 2024-04-05T12:34:11Z GET /v1/generate 504 "timeout" src=10.2.7.44
```

eng-gw: noticing amplification pattern: single origin client (10.2.7.44) opened lots of concurrent connections, fanout to multiple backends. QPS from that IP jumped x15. Could be retry storm from an internal LB or buggy client.

ops_liz: I'm scaling edgepool-7 +2 nodes and enabling circuit breaker thresholds on that pool to 80% to stop tail amplification. Giving commands: `rbctl pool scale edgepool-7 +2` and `rbctl pool set edgepool-7 circuit_breaker=0.8`

oncall-ben: starting a traffic steer for /v1/generate to us-east to relieve usw1: `rbctl steer --route /v1/generate --from-region us-west --to-region us-east --duration 30m` — doing 100% for now, will ramp if stable.

incident-bot: Incident severity set to P1. Pages escalated to oncall rotation and Eng-GW oncall. Incident channel pinned.

jamie: can we TTL-bump cached model results for a few minutes to reduce origin hits? might buy time while we drain.

eng-gw: deployed quick config change on usw1 proxies: reduced HTTP/2 concurrent streams to 50 and lowered upstream connection pool size. Config diff:```
http2_max_concurrent_streams 50;
upstream keepalive 16;
```
rolled in canary to 2 proxies.

cs-ken: customer impact update: B2B customers in US-West seeing elevated client-side errors, estimates ~20-60% increase depending on route. Notifying our top 10 accounts now (DMs sent).

mike: digging into LBs — seeing many healthcheck retries and internal client retries hitting edgepool-7 which amplifies via fanout. Logs show: `retry_count=8` from internal LB. If we reduce retry policy at LB we should cut amplification.

ops_liz: changed LB retry config: `max_retries: 1` and disabled aggressive backoff for target group usw1-targets. Also draining suspect origin 10.2.7.44 from rotation.

oncall-ben: after steering + config changes, errors on /v1/generate dropped from ~35% -> ~8% over 6 minutes. Latency also improving. Keeping traffic steer for 30m and monitoring.

sre_maria: creating incident doc and temporary runbook. Assigning follow-up: @jamie to investigate retry sources, @eng-gw to prepare a hardening patch for connection pooling.

eng-gw: plan for follow-up patch: lower default keepalive time, reduce upstream queue depth and add better per-connection backpressure. We'll run a canary tomorrow.

jamie: will check internal telemetry to identify which service/healthcheck misconfiguration triggered the retries; maybe a bad deploy rolled a healthcheck change.

cs-ken: sent external status update to customers: short note about regional errors and mitigation in progress, reference incident id and ETA.

mike: confirm root cause hypothesis: internal LB misconfig -> retry storm -> edge proxy queueing -> upstream 503s. Will include log snippets in postmortem.

ops_liz: continuing to drain edgepool-7, scaling replacement capacity in us-west to keep throughput while draining.

oncall-ben: handing off to night SRE @sre_maria at 1712346111 — monitoring dashboards, alert thresholds lowered to catch regression (>10% 5xx). Handoff notes: traffic is steered, retry policy relaxed at LB, edgepool drained, patch queued.

sre_maria: ack. I'll watch for regressions and compile a customer impact timeline. We should schedule a postmortem and include mitigation checklist (steer traffic, scale pool, disable retries, drain offending origin).

incident-bot: Incident updated: status=monitoring, current_impact=partial (us-west degraded for ~20-30m), next_update in 15m.

oncall-ben: thanks team — closing active pages for me. Please escalate if error rate climbs above 10% again. :thumbsup:
